lesson.focus: group guided reading of the reader 'Amabaso okutya okunempilo' (presents of healthy food) with one group on the mat; each learner reads sentences aloud

summary_en: The recording opens with the teacher telling the class to keep reading while one named group comes to the mat; settling the group takes about two and a half minutes, then the teacher asks the group to recall what to do with an unknown word and to read the book title. Learners then read sentences aloud one at a time while the teacher listens, prompts re-reading from the start of a sentence, gives first-syllable cues and praises one learner for going back and re-reading a whole sentence; the session closes with a reminder to read fluently and the books being collected. The recording does not show what the rest of the class was doing independently, how this group's text level was chosen, any notes the teacher keeps for the next session, or any discussion of what the story means; an unrehearsed session would also need to show these. One possible slip (turns 177-181, 'ngobusi' vs 'ngobuso') is treated as a transcription question, not as a learner error.
scope_en: Rumi coached only what the recording shows in class (the teacher and learners). Narration over the film is in the transcript but is not treated as evidence that a step happened. The recording is an edited training film, so a step it does not show may still have happened.

culture.name: Ukuhlola ukuqonda komfundi ngamnye
culture.note_en: The teacher listens to one reader at a time and responds to each; the checks are about accurate decoding, and no record of what each learner needs is seen.

evidence.en: So I want to listen to them now

evidence.quote: Yifunde yonke ke ngoku la esasivakalisi. Qale qaleni.
evidence.en: Read that whole sentence now. Start from the beginning.

positives.en: Every learner in the group gets their own reading turn while the others follow, so the teacher can hear each child's reading rather than a chorus.
When a learner stumbles, the teacher sends them back to the start of the sentence and lets them read it whole again, which keeps the learner doing the decoding work.
The teacher names the exact strategy a learner used (going back and re-reading the whole sentence) in front of the group, so the others learn what to do when they get stuck.
Before reading, the teacher has the group recall what to do with an unknown word, linking this session to the earlier shared reading.

blockages.en: Reading well is framed as reading fast ('sifuna ukhawulezisa xa sifunda'), and only one meaning question is asked during the whole session. Effect: learners may come to believe that good reading means speed, and slower decoders hear their halting reading imitated as the thing to avoid, while no one checks whether the group understood the story. Catch-up: after each learner's sentence, ask one short meaning question ('yitsho ngamazwi akho') and close with a two-sentence retell of the page.

Moving the group to the mat and settling places takes about two and a half minutes before the first sentence is read, and later the teacher warns that only two minutes are left. Effect: fewer reading turns and less time for the slowest readers, who need the most practice. Catch-up: a fixed mat routine (group leader brings the books, set places, pencils left at desks) practised until the group starts reading within a minute.

level_of_change.en: Focus skill: checking meaning (not only speed and accuracy) during group guided reading. The teacher already runs individual turns and decoding prompts, and says they want fluent reading, but the session shows no routine for meaning checks, which suggests knowing the goal without yet having the moves (level 2). One recorded session is thin evidence, so confidence is low. Matching coach move: demonstrate a short guided reading turn step by step, with one 'say it in your own words' question after each sentence, then plan the next session together.

goal.lang: Kwiseshoni elandelayo yokufunda ngokukhokelwa eqeleni, emva kokuba umntwana ngamnye efunde isivakalisi sakhe, ndiza kubuza umbuzo omnye omfutshane malunga nentsingiselo.
goal.en: In the next group guided reading session, after each child reads their sentence, I will ask one short question about its meaning.

reality.lang: Ngoku umntwana ngamnye uyafunda kwaye ndiyamnceda ukuba aphinde afunde, kodwa ndibuza kanye kuphela malunga nentsingiselo, kwaye ndigxininisa ekukhawulezeni.
reality.en: Right now each child reads and I help them re-read, but I ask about meaning only once, and I stress reading fast.

options.lang: Ndingabuza ndithi yitsho ngamazwi akho; ndingacela iqela ukuba libalise ibali ngamafutshane ekupheleni; okanye ndingalungiselela imibuzo emibini ngaphambi kweseshoni.
options.en: I could ask 'say it in your own words'; I could ask the group to retell the story briefly at the end; or I could prepare two questions before the session.

way_forward.lang: Ngomso ndiza kubhala imibuzo emibini emfutshane kwincwadi yeqela, ndiyibuze ngexesha lokufunda, kwaye ndibhale amagama abantwana abaye bayiqonda.
way_forward.en: Tomorrow I will write two short questions for the group's book, ask them during reading, and note which children understood.

questions.lang: Xa uthi kubantwana sifuna ukukhawulezisa xa sifunda, ucinga ukuba bayiqonda njani into ethi ukufunda kakuhle?
questions.en: When you tell the children we want to speed up when we read, how do you think they understand what reading well means?

questions.lang: Xa wancoma umntwana owabuyela ekuqaleni kwesivakalisi, yintoni obona ngathi abanye abantwana bayifundile kuloo mzuzu?
questions.en: When you praised the child who went back to the start of the sentence, what do you think the other children learnt in that moment?

questions.lang: Ungathanda ukuba ukuza kweqela emethini kubonakale njani, ukuze ixesha elininzi lisetyenziselwe ukufunda?
questions.en: How would you like the group's arrival at the mat to look, so that more of the time is used for reading?

debrief_plan.coach_says: Enkosi ngokundamkela kwiseshoni yakho yokufunda neqela. Ndingabelana nawe ngezinto endizibonileyo?
debrief_plan.en: Thank you for welcoming me to your group reading session. May I share with you what I saw?

debrief_plan.coach_says: Ndibone ukuba umntwana ngamnye ufunde ngokwakhe, kwaye xa umntwana ebebambekile umbuyisele ekuqaleni kwesivakalisi, wamncoma xa ebuyela emva. Ndiphinde ndabona ukuba ugxininise kakhulu ekukhawulezeni, kwaye ubuze kanye kuphela malunga nentsingiselo yegama.
debrief_plan.en: I saw that each child read on their own, and when a child got stuck you sent them back to the start of the sentence and praised them for going back. I also saw that you stressed speed a lot, and asked about meaning only once, about one word.

debrief_plan.coach_says: Xa abantwana besiva ukuba ukufunda kakuhle kukukhawuleza, banokufunda amagama ngaphandle kokuqonda ibali, kwaye abo bafunda kancinci banokuziva beneentloni.
debrief_plan.en: When children hear that reading well means being fast, they may read the words without understanding the story, and those who read slowly may feel embarrassed.

debrief_plan.coach_says: Ndingathanda ukuva umbono wakho. Wena ufuna ukuba abantwana bakho bazi ntoni ngokufunda ngokugeleza?
debrief_plan.en: I would like to hear your view. What do you want your children to know about fluent reading?

debrief_plan.coach_says: Masivumelane ngento enye: emva kwesivakalisi ngasinye, ubuze umbuzo omnye omfutshane, umzekelo yitsho ngamazwi akho. Ndingeza ndikubonise kwiseshoni elandelayo, size sithethe kwakhona emva koko.
debrief_plan.en: Let us agree on one thing: after each sentence, ask one short question, for example 'say it in your own words'. I can come and show you in the next session, and we can talk again afterwards.

next_step.lang: Emva kokuba umntwana ngamnye efunde isivakalisi sakhe, buza umbuzo omnye omfutshane ngentsingiselo, umzekelo yitsho ngamazwi akho, phambi kokuba uqhubele komnye umntwana.
next_step.en: After each child reads their sentence, ask one short meaning question, for example 'say it in your own words', before moving to the next child.

accuracy.label: measured
accuracy.line: These numbers measure Rumi: whether its quotes are really in the lesson, whether it filled every part of the report, and whether it reads the lesson the same way three times. They do not grade the teacher.

model: Lesson-step and classroom-culture judgements by Claude Opus 5.5, the stricter of the two models we compared. Three independent readings of the same transcript; the report shows the median reading, with each item's status taken from the majority.
